newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan welcomes exclusion from U.S. watchlist.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan welcomes exclusion from U.S. watchlist.

text.p: Taiwan on Thursday welcomed a U.S. decision to take Taipei off its "watchlists" of countries deemed lax on protecting intellectual property rights.

"We are pleased to learn of this. This shows our efforts to address intellectual property rights problems have been acknowledged by the United States," Lin Yi-fu, director of the Board of Foreign Trade, told Reuters.
"We will continue these efforts," he said.

The U.S. Trade Representative released its Special 301 annual review of how well countries were protecting intellectual property rights on Wednesday. Taiwan was not on any of the review's three watchlists for the first time since 1989.
A persistently poor record would merit possible U.S. trade sanctions.
The United States is one of Taipei's major trading partners despite the absence of diplomatic relations.
